summary.headline: Motherson posted record Q1 FY27 revenue, up 17% YoY, with EBITDA up 26% and margin up 60 bps despite copper, polymer and freight inflation.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 17% YoY and 3% QoQ to a record, and Q1 revenue exceeded Q4 FY26, which management said is unusual since Q1 normally declines sequentially. EBITDA rose 26% YoY with margin up 60 bps, led by the modules and polymer (MPP) business after European restructuring. Normalized PAT grew 55% YoY, with no one-off items in the quarter. Management flagged copper up 40% YoY, polymer prices in Germany up 55% YoY, and the World Container Index up 40% YoY as headwinds, with pass-through lagging by 1-2 quarters. Capex of INR 1,614 crore was in line with the INR 6,000 crore full-year guidance, and leverage fell to 0.8x.

financial_highlights.value: Record quarterly revenue (value not stated in call)

financial_highlights.change: +55% YoY; reported PAT +102% YoY adjusted for base-quarter normalization
All-time low; policy ceiling 2.5x, internal aspiration below 1.5x
+31% YoY, driven by India and North American CV recovery
Over +20% YoY; order book up more than 17% since FY26 end

segments.name: Wiring harness
segments.commentary: Revenue up 31% YoY on strong India momentum and recovery in North American commercial vehicles. Margin impact from copper was muted, per management, helped by diversification and cost actions; 4-5% QoQ copper impact globally, larger in India due to rupee depreciation.

segments.name: Modules and polymer (MPP)
segments.commentary: Margin improvement was the main driver of group EBITDA margin expansion, supported by footprint restructuring over the last 1.5 years. Management did not quantify the commodity headwind offset; plastics pass-through is settled annually, mostly in Q4.

segments.name: Vision systems
segments.commentary: Grew in line with industry; polymer cost inflation in Germany hit the division, but margins were held flat to improving. Management highlighted the mirror business as a high free-cash-flow generator.

segments.name: Consumer electronics (glass, emerging business)
segments.commentary: Scaling with new facilities; the third plant is on track for commissioning in Q3 FY27 at 40 million units annual capacity. Total project capex is about INR 7,500 crore, with about one-third spent so far. Management said FY26 revenue was about INR 1,300 crore at 8% EBITDA margin (per analyst question).

segments.name: Aerospace (emerging business)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew over 20% YoY and the order book rose more than 17% since FY26 end.

segments.name: Integrated assemblies and emerging businesses
segments.commentary: Clubbed together at an early stage, so quarterly margins are volatile due to ramp-ups and new launches. Management plans to break out consumer electronics and others once they are meaningful in size.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 capex guidance of INR 6,000 crore, plus or minus 10%; Q1 spend was in line with this.
13 facilities at various stages of development, of which 10 are expected to become operational during FY27.
Consumer electronics third plant commissioning targeted in Q3 FY27 (management pushed to try for later in the calendar year); full-scale capacity of 40 million units annually, achieved over time.

Acquired Yutaka Giken and Nexans Autoelectric (completed July 2026); together they should add close to USD 2 billion annualized revenue. Newly acquired businesses are below industry margins for now, with improvement targeted over the midterm.
Management targets 40% ROCE across businesses; Q4 expected to show the strongest margin performance as commodity and volume compensation is netted.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex of INR 1,614 crore, 52% of quarter EBITDA, covering growth, backward integration and maintenance.

Consumer electronics: Phase 1 capex to complete this year; a formal inauguration is planned in a couple of months for what management called the largest facility in the group. Third facility capex about INR 6,500 crore over 3 years, with 40 million units annual capacity at full scale.
Consumer electronics total project capex about INR 7,500 crore (GF1, GF2, GF3), with about one-third incurred; the balance over the next 2-3 years.
Consumer electronics JV: partner holds 10% equity and can go up to 49%; Motherson funds 90%. Management said there is no indication the partner plans to increase its stake.
Consumer electronics existing two facilities are prototype-scale; the third plant capacity is already fully committed to a customer, per management.
demand_pricing: Global light vehicle production declined 1.8% YoY in the quarter; China fell 3.1%; South Asia led by India grew strongly.
North American commercial vehicle industry grew an estimated 5.4% YoY; management expects CV growth to remain favorable through FY27.
Copper prices up 40% YoY and 4% QoQ, following 13% and 16% QoQ rises in Q3 and Q4 FY26; pass-through lags by 1-2 quarters (3-6 months per CFO commentary).
German polymer prices up 55% YoY and 66% QoQ; World Container Index up 40% YoY and 83% QoQ, with additional logistics costs incurred to meet delivery timelines.
China: the business is shifting toward local Chinese OEMs; management says international OEM share holds, and it is building supply relationships with Chinese OEMs that are expanding into Europe.

qa_highlights.question: What are the annualized revenue and margins for the newly acquired Yutaka and Nexans businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Together they should contribute close to USD 2 billion annualized revenue. Margins are not yet at the industry benchmark of about 11%, but management expects improvement over the midterm.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full capex and funding structure for consumer electronics, and how much revenue can 40 million units generate?
qa_highlights.answer: Total capex is about INR 7,500 crore, with the JV partner at 10% equity and Motherson funding 90%. Management declined to give revenue guidance and asked for two more quarters of patience.

qa_highlights.question: How much did commodity headwinds cost in Q1 and how much did restructuring offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify the split. Plastics pass-through is settled periodically, mostly at year-end, so the full effect is expected in Q4. Restructuring benefits are described as meaningful.

qa_highlights.question: Why is wiring harness margin impact from copper so small?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the global impact is about 4-5% QoQ with a 3-6 month pass-through lag. The India impact is larger due to rupee depreciation. Diversification and cost actions in international operations offset the rest.

qa_highlights.question: Will the emerging businesses be separately listed, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said listing is on the cards, possibly within the 5-year plan. Timing depends on execution, and value unlock could come as early as FY28. No firm date was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a regulatory tailwind for vision systems from AIS 184 driver drowsiness rules in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajat Jain said new regulations are a tailwind. The Autocruis acquisition brings interior digital mirrors and driver monitoring, subject to homologation in India.

risks_watch: Copper, polymer and freight costs are still rising; pass-through is lagged and the full impact may only show in Q4, so Q2 margins may come under pressure.
Consumer electronics ramp depends on winning programs; the third plant commissioning slipped from earlier guidance, and management gave no revenue figures.
Newly acquired businesses (Nexans, Yutaka) are below industry margins and need integration and synergy delivery.
The emerging business segment is reported as a club of early-stage businesses, which limits transparency until they are broken out.
Health and medical revenue has declined over three years, with losses rising; the Chennai plant is starting up.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and balance sheet, but guarded on the timing and size of consumer electronics revenue and on quantifying commodity offsets. Management repeatedly asked investors for patience of two more quarters.
key_quotes: We are pleased to report our highest-ever quarterly revenue in Q1 FY '27, driven by robust performance across our businesses.
Our leverage ratio is now at an all -time low of 0.8x, well within our financial policy ceiling of 2.5x and our internal aspiration of staying below 1.5x.

But I think the reduction in the headcount and the optimization of the footprint, you're seeing those benefits which are meaningful that even with such high impact of the commodity prices and logistics for all the issues that are happening in the world that we've been able to maintain, and of course, improve some of our performance in the margins.
So please just be a little bit more patient with us. I know we've kept you guys waiting for some of this, but please believe me, it's worth it.

adds.what: Consumer electronics third plant (GF3), 40 million units/yr at full scale; capacity already fully committed to a customer
13 facilities at various stages of development, 10 expected operational during FY27

growth.why: No numeric FY27 revenue guidance; growth rests on 10 of 13 facilities coming online in FY27, the consumer electronics GF3 plant (40m units, Q3 FY27 target, fully committed to a customer) and ~USD 2bn annualized revenue from the Yutaka Giken and Nexans Autoelectric acquisitions, with aerospace orders up 17%.
